# OmniPackage

> {{ site.description | strip_newlines }}

OmniPackage is an open source command-line tool. It builds RPM, DEB, and pacman packages for many Linux distros and uploads them to a repository you host yourself, in S3-compatible storage or a local directory. Users install your software with apt, dnf, zypper, or pacman, the same way they install packages from their distro. You do not need an account or a subscription.

## How it works

1. Set up: `omnipackage init` creates the files needed to build RPM, DEB, and pacman packages.
2. Release: `omnipackage release` builds each package in a container with the target distro (`rpmbuild`, `dpkg-buildpackage`, or `makepkg`), so the package uses that distro's own libraries. It signs the packages with your GPG key and uploads them to your S3 bucket or local directory. That storage is the repository.
3. Share: OmniPackage also creates an install page with commands to copy. Users run them once to add the repository, then get updates with their usual package manager.

## Supported distros

openSUSE (Leap and Tumbleweed), Fedora (including Rawhide), Debian (stable, testing, unstable), Ubuntu, Mageia, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, Arch Linux, and Manjaro. The full, current list is in [`distros.yml`]({{ site.github_repo_url }}/blob/master/src/distros.yml) in the source repository.

Packages are built for the CPU architecture of the build machine, x86_64 or ARM64. Arch Linux supports only x86_64, and Manjaro no longer updates its ARM repositories.

## Key facts

- Docker is not required. OmniPackage works with Podman or Docker and uses Podman if both are installed. Use `--container-runtime` to choose one.
- Your repository can store closed-source packages.
- Any S3-compatible storage works, for example AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, or MinIO. Cloudflare R2 is recommended because it is the most tested and has no fees for download traffic.
- OmniPackage does not build Flatpak, Snap, AppImage, or Nix packages, and does not publish to AUR.
- OmniPackage does not sandbox apps. Packages get the same permissions as any other system package.

## Inspiration and related projects

- [openSUSE Build Service](https://build.opensuse.org/): the main inspiration
- Flatpak and Snap: ship their own runtimes, so apps do not depend on distro libraries
- AppImage: one file that includes all dependencies
- AUR: build recipes shared by Arch Linux users
- Nix: a different approach to packaging
